---
title: "Uncertainty — Labs"
---

Six hands-on notebooks in two tracks, mirroring the
[dependence labs](../../dependence/labs/index.qmd).  The verb is **propagate**:
sample the joint, push it through, and report honest uncertainty.

## Learn-the-Tool Track

| Lab | Topic |
|-----|-------|
| [Tool 1 — Independent fails](lab-tool1-independent-fail.qmd) | why per-marginal sampling destroys the joint |
| [Tool 2 — Gaussian Monte-Carlo](lab-tool2-gaussian-mc.qmd) | right correlation, thin tails; the VaR gap |
| [Tool 3 — Predictive bands](lab-tool3-bands.qmd) | neural-net uncertainty: an NLL net's σ(x) + a deep ensemble |

## Do-the-Job Track

| Lab | Deliverable |
|-----|-------------|
| [Job A — Stress scenarios](lab-jobA-stress-scenarios.qmd) | RBIG scenarios with the real joint tail |
| [Job B — Portfolio VaR](lab-jobB-portfolio-var.qmd) | propagate returns to a 1% VaR, three ways |
| [Job C — Predict from noise](lab-jobC-predict-from-noise.qmd) | a calibrated, regime-aware interval from forecast volatility |

## Shared Setup

```python
import sys, pathlib
sys.path.insert(0, str(pathlib.Path.cwd() / "src"))
from lectures import plotting, datasets
from rbig import AnnealedRBIG
from lectures.measures import cocrash_fraction
plotting.set_style("notes")

# the prediction-band labs train small Keras nets (CPU JAX backend)
import os
os.environ["KERAS_BACKEND"] = "jax"   # set BEFORE importing keras
import keras
```

The do-the-job labs load real returns with `datasets.load_returns()`.
